main_text.p: Quod sortis ratione supputata, Et Cleri titulo magis recepto, Christi Ecclesia tota continetur.
Quanto rectius ergo nominantur Ista similiola Antichristiana Illo a vermiculo aluearium Quem ηλιηρον etiam vocant Athena.

Nasci hunc inter apes probauit vsus, Et rerum experientia abditarum, Qui vires vbi sumpsit ad nocendum, Ingentesque animos, repente totis Spargit tabificum fauis venenum. Hinc porro est apibus lues acerba, Quum dulces animas, suosque fœtus Linquunt ante diem furente morbo.
Victor denique gloriosus ille, Tanquam re bene fortiterque gesta, Assumptis humeros reuicit alis.

Sed lucem æthereram & diem perosus, Tantum nocte volat tenebricosa: Et quodcunque habet obuium πυρφυγης Infestat subito impetitq; lumen, Donec conciderit perustus igne, Quem circumuolitat premente fato.
An non huic similes videntur esse, Quos nunc Papa suo ordinis sequaces Cleri voce putat beare solos, Tantum significatione falsus?

page.notes: The first letters of several lines are large decorative initials, read here as Q, A, etc. Line "Quos" is partly obscured by a small ink mark and is read as Quos. The Greek words "ηλιηρον" (rendered with the nearest Greek letters) and "πυρφυγης" are printed in Greek and are doubtful in their accents. Faint show-through of the reverse page is present and has been ignored. The words "Ista similiola" and "Athena" are uncertain in the scan. The word "perosus" and the spelling "Allumptis" have been read as printed. The final "In" at the foot right is a catchword.
